note: Standard questions used when the model is unavailable or returns too few, grouped by the families panels use (founder round 20, from a 100 question bank and an NHS receptionist set). The first question is always 'Tell me about yourself.' and the last 'Do you have any questions for us?' (added by code).

opening.question: Tell me about yourself.
opening.why: Almost every interview opens with this. Keep it to about a minute: who you are, your strongest proof for this job, and why this role.

standard.question: Why have you applied for this position?
standard.why: Motivation question. Connect your interests, skills and experience to what the role does.

standard.question: What do you understand about the main responsibilities of this role?
standard.why: Role question. Name the main duties from the post and how you'd handle them.

standard.question: How has your experience so far prepared you for this position?
standard.why: Motivation question. Pick two things from your CV that match the job.

standard.question: Describe a time you showed honesty and integrity.
standard.why: Values question. Use a real example and say what you did and why.

standard.question: Tell us about a time you dealt with a difficult or upset person.
standard.why: Communication question. Say how you stayed calm, listened and solved it.

standard.question: Describe a time you handled confidential or sensitive information.
standard.why: Confidentiality question, common where the role sees personal or financial details.

standard.question: Tell us about a time you managed several urgent tasks at once.
standard.why: Organisation question. Show how you decided what came first.

standard.question: Describe a time you worked well as part of a team.
standard.why: Teamwork question, asked at every level.

standard.question: Tell us about a mistake you made and what you learned from it.
standard.why: Competency question. Own it, say what you fixed, and what you do differently now.

standard.question: What would you do if two colleagues gave you conflicting instructions about an urgent task?
standard.why: Situational question. Say what you'd do, why, and when you'd ask a manager.

standard.question: How would you respond if you noticed an error that could affect the outcome of your work?
standard.why: Situational question about accuracy and owning problems early.

standard.question: What would you hope to achieve in your first three to six months here?
standard.why: Career question. Show you've thought about learning the role and adding value.

standard.question: Why should we choose you over other candidates?
standard.why: Closing question. Sum up your strongest proof for this job in a minute.

closing.question: Do you have any questions for us?
closing.why: Closing question. Have two or three ready about the role, the team or training. It shows real interest.
